story_title: Windows Task Scheduler privilege escalation CVE-2024-49039 listed in the KEV catalog

provenance.note: Live end-to-end holdout v5 candidate. KEV membership verified against the seeded live CISA catalog feed on 2026-10-10 (Microsoft Windows Task Scheduler EoP). Keywords are the official product words from the KEV entry and the NVD description (OR semantics). Disjoint from both development datasets and all consumed holdouts (v1/v2/v3/v4). Independent review: glm-5.3-flash=high:CVE-2024-49039 is the Windows Task Scheduler Elevation of Privilege vulnerability; MSRC and NVD name Windows/Task Scheduler as affected product, and CISA added it to the KEV catalog (vendorProject Microsoft, product Windows) in December 2024. known_exploited=yes is supported and row_contains 'windows'/'task scheduler' matches official naming; propose is conservative since the advisory grounds affected products.; deepseek-v4.1-flash=high:CVE-2024-49039 is a Windows Task Scheduler elevation-of-privilege vulnerability documented by MSRC and NVD, and it is a genuine CISA KEV entry, so known_exploited=yes is correct; row_contains 'windows'/'task scheduler' match products named in the official advisory, and the allowed set (propose plus insufficient_evidence with preserved unknowns, min_rows 0) is conservative and permissible.; kimi-k2.8-preview=high:CVE-2024-49039 is a Windows Task Scheduler elevation of privilege publicly disclosed by Microsoft as exploited in the wild (Nov 2024 Patch Tuesday) and added to the CISA KEV catalog; the MSRC advisory names 'Windows Task Scheduler', matching row_contains keywords 'windows' and 'task scheduler'; the expected set of propose plus insufficient_evidence with preserved unknowns is conservative, and known_exploited=yes is grounded in genuine KEV membership.
